messages:
Sam - AcmeCorp: hey support — our embeddings queries started failing right after we applied the pinned model update this morning. indexer throws a hard error during similarity search. getting: "400 Bad Request: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024". this is blocking search on prod. ticket #INC-5921
Maya S: hey Sam, sorry about that — we're on it. can you share the request id / sample payload and the model id you pinned? also which client lib/version are you using? :eyes:
Sam - AcmeCorp: request_id: rqd_8b7f2c9a, model: embed-alpha-2026-03, client: python-sdk 1.3.2. sample request (truncated):
```json
{"input":"how do i reset password","model":"embed-alpha-2026-03"}
```
Maya S: thanks. quick check — is your index expecting 1536 vectors from prior model? looks like the new model is returning 1024. can you confirm what you had before the pin? any reindexing since last deploy?
Sam - AcmeCorp: we were on embed-alpha-v1 (1536). we pinned to embed-alpha-2026-03 yesterday during a maintenance window thinking it was a drop-in. no reindex done.
Maya S: ok that explains it. i'm escalating to eng-runtime and ml-infra. looping in @Liam R and @Jason K. will gather repro steps + suggested mitigation.
Liam R: pinged. quick note: some of the newer embedding variants are reshaped/architecturally different and return 1024 by design. pinning behavior can cause client->model mismatch if alias pointed to new artifact. investigating routing + metadata checks.
Jason K: i pulled the model metadata for embed-alpha-2026-03: GET /v1/models/embed-alpha-2026-03/metadata => {"embedding_dim":"1024","architecture":"embed-transformer-8"}
Jason K: and for embed-alpha-v1: {"embedding_dim":"1536","architecture":"embed-transformer-12"}
Maya S: reproducible locally: curl to hosted endpoint returns error when vector store expects 1536. example response:
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024"
}
```
Maya S: root cause summary: model upgrade changed vector dimensionality. clients / index were not re-embedded and index schema expected previous dim. pinning switched traffic to new artifact without reindexing.
Sam - AcmeCorp: ugh. what's the fastest way to unstick prod? can we point alias back to old model while we re-embed? or is there a runtime shim that can pad/truncate?
Liam R: short term options:
- revert alias/pin to embed-alpha-v1 (recommended) — that'll restore expected dims immediately. needs a quick change in your pin/alias config or we can do it from our side with customer consent.
- run a conversion shim that pads 1024 -> 1536, but that will likely degrade nearest-neighbor accuracy (not recommended for production search quality).
- re-embed corpus to 1024 using new model (best long-term) — this is heavier work but fixes permanently.
Maya S: Jason, can you confirm we have tooling to flip model alias for a customer's pinned version quickly and any audit/SLA implications?
Jason K: yes — we can create a temporary alias rollback within the customer's Dedicated/Private config or suggest a pin update in Hosted. it requires ticket authorization and a short maintenance window to make the change and validate. no SLA penalty for rollback itself.
Maya S: Sam — if you want us to flip the alias back to embed-alpha-v1, confirm and I'll open an authorization request. also please share an approximate size of your corpus (# vectors) and whether reindexing during the day is possible.
Sam - AcmeCorp: corpus ~2.4M vectors. we'd prefer alias rollback for immediate relief and then plan an overnight reindex to new dims. can you do rollback today? :pray:
Maya S: noted. opening authorization now. @OpsBot creating change request.
OpsBot: Change request CR-7821 created for customer AcmeCorp: rollback alias for embed model. Owner: support. ETA: 30m. :white_check_mark:
Liam R: a couple of technical notes for the reindex plan:
- re-embedding 2.4M vectors at ~200/sec will take ~3.3 hours (plus ingestion). consider using batch re-embed tool with parallel workers on Dedicated.
- if you want zero-downtime reindex, we can do dual-index roll: build new index with 1024 vectors + shadow traffic, then switch alias at cutover.
- batching and kv-cache behavior is unrelated to dim, but early batching misconfigs can increase tail latency during reindex.
Maya S: internal next steps: (1) wait for Sam confirmation to proceed with rollback (auth), (2) validate alias switch on staging, (3) flip in prod and smoke-test similarity queries, (4) handoff reindex runbook to AcmeCorp for overnight run.
Sam - AcmeCorp: auth sent via support portal. please proceed with rollback and ping when done.
Jason K: rolling back alias now. changing embed-alias:embed-alpha -> embed-alpha-v1. will post logs.
Jason K: DONE — alias rollback completed at 1778881298. validation checks: ran 10 sample queries against index — all returning expected vector lengths and no dimension errors.
Maya S: Sam, can you validate from your side? run a couple of search queries and confirm results.
Sam - AcmeCorp: confirmed — search responses working, no 400s. massive relief, thanks team :tada:
Maya S: great. follow-up actions for us and customer:
- Sam: schedule reindex overnight to migrate corpus to 1024 (or keep pinned older model if you want to stay on 1536 long-term).
- Support/Eng: add a safety check in pin/alias flow to warn when model embedding_dim differs from previous pinned artifact (we'll file a small feature ticket).
Liam R: filing feature ticket: FEAT-3442 "embed-pin-dim-warning" — warn in console + API when a pin would change vector dimensionality; include checkbox to allow destructive change and reminder about reindexing.
Maya S: closing thread once reindex plan is confirmed. marking as resolved for immediate outage.
Sam - AcmeCorp: will schedule reindex and follow up if anything else pops up. thanks again everyone.
Maya S: resolved for now — leaving notes on the ticket and linking FEAT-3442. :white_check_mark:
